```{r setup, echo=FALSE, cache=FALSE, warning=FALSE, message=FALSE}
library(ggplot2) #plotting
library(envreportutils) #for theme_soe and theme_soe_facet
library(scales) #for label = comma
library(forcats) # fct_rev() for stacking order
library(RColorBrewer) #for colour palette
library(dplyr)
library(knitr) #for rendering the PDF
library(here)
library(reshape2)
library(plotly)
library(targets)
library(ggiraph)
library(readr)
library(glue)
library(bcmaps)
library(here)
library(shiny)


opts_chunk$set(echo=FALSE, cache=FALSE, warning=FALSE, message=FALSE, error=FALSE, fig.height=3.5, fig.width = 8, fig.align = 'center')
theme_print <-   theme(axis.text.y = element_text(size = 8),
                       axis.text.x = element_text(size = 8),
                       axis.title.y = element_text(size = 10,
                                                   margin = margin(t = 0, r = 10,
                                                                   b = 0, l = 0,
                                                                   unit = "pt")),
                       plot.title = element_text(size = 10, hjust = 0.5),
                       plot.margin = unit(c(6,6,6,2),"mm"))
#theme for plots with integrated labels
theme_summary <- theme(axis.text.y = element_text(size = 8),
                       axis.text.x = element_text(size = 8),
                       axis.title.y = element_text(size = 10,
                                                   margin = margin(t = 0, r = 10,
                                                                   b = 0, l = 0,
                                                                   unit = "pt")),
                       plot.title = element_text(size = 10, hjust = 0.5),
                       plot.margin = unit(c(0.5,3.5,0.5,0.5), "cm"))

#knitr::opts_knit$set(root.dir = 'C:/tmp/protected-lands-and-water-indicator')

is_html <- knitr::is_html_output()
is_pdf <- knitr::is_latex_output()
if (is_pdf) opts_chunk$set(fig.width = 6.5)

total_prot_area <- read_rds(paste0(here::here(), "/out/total_prot_area.rds"))

pa_total <- total_prot_area %>% 
  group_by(park_type, type) %>% 
  dplyr::filter(date == 2024) %>% 
  select(summary_total)

land_pa <- pa_total %>% 
  dplyr::filter(park_type == "PA"&type =="land")

land_oecm <- pa_total %>% 
  dplyr::filter(park_type == "OECM"&type =="land")

water_pa <- pa_total %>% 
  dplyr::filter(park_type == "PA"&type =="water")

water_oecm <- pa_total %>% 
  dplyr::filter(park_type == "OECM"&type =="water")

land_total <- round(land_pa$summary_total + land_oecm$summary_total, digits=1)

water_total <- round(water_pa$summary_total + water_oecm$summary_total, digits=1) #watertotal

n_ecoregions <- read_rds(paste0(here::here(), "/out/eco_simp.rds")) %>%
                as.data.frame() %>%
                count(type)

land_highest_percent <- read_rds(paste0(here::here(), "/out/pa_eco_sum.rds")) %>%
                        filter(date == 2024 & type == "land") %>%
                        select(ecoregion_code, ecoregion_name, type, p_region) %>%
                        distinct() %>%
                        slice_max(p_region, n = 2) %>%
                        as.data.frame()

land_lowest_percent <-  read_rds(paste0(here::here(), "/out/pa_eco_sum.rds")) %>%
                        filter(date == 2024 & type == "land") %>%
                        select(ecoregion_code, ecoregion_name, type, p_region) %>%
                        distinct() %>%
                        slice_min(p_region, n = 2) %>%
                        as.data.frame()

water_highest_percent <- read_rds(paste0(here::here(), "/out/pa_eco_sum.rds")) %>%
                         filter(date == 2024 & type == "water") %>%
                         select(ecoregion_code, ecoregion_name, park_type, type, p_type, p_region) %>%
                         distinct() %>%
                         slice_max(p_region, n = 1) %>%
                         as.data.frame()

water_lowest_percent <-  read_rds(paste0(here::here(), "/out/pa_eco_sum.rds")) %>%
                         filter(date == 2024 & type == "water") %>%
                         select(ecoregion_code, ecoregion_name, type, p_region) %>%
                         distinct() %>%
                         slice_min(p_region, n = 1) %>%
                         as.data.frame()

zone_high_elevation_percent <- read_rds(paste0(here::here(), "/out/bec_area.rds")) %>%
                filter(zone_name == "Boreal Altai Fescue Alpine"|
                zone_name == "Interior Mountain-heather Alpine") %>%
                mutate(total_bc = bcmaps::bc_area(),
                       bec_rep = total/total_bc)

zone_highest_percent <- read_rds(paste0(here::here(), "/out/bec_area.rds")) %>%
                mutate(total_bc = bcmaps::bc_area(),
                       bec_rep = total/total_bc) %>%
                slice_max(bec_rep, n = 1) %>%
                as.data.frame()

zone_lowest_percent <- read_rds(paste0(here::here(), "/out/bec_area.rds")) %>%
                       slice_min(perc_zone, n = 1) %>%
                       as.data.frame()
```

* Conserved lands and waters are legally established areas set aside to protect nature and cultural values. Conserved areas, particularly BC Parks, are well-used by British Columbians with 6 in 10 people visiting a provincial park each year^1^.
* **Conserved lands and water cover `r land_total`% of B.C.'s terrestrial areas and inland water and `r water_total`% of coastal and marine areas.** B.C.'s network of conserved lands and waters contribute to the [Convention on Biological Diversity Aichi Target 11](https://www.cbd.int/aichi-targets/target/11)^2^ commitments to set aside 17% of terrestrial areas and 10% of marine areas by 2020. 
* B.C.'s conserved areas include marine and terrestrial protected areas [(PAs)](https://www.canada.ca/en/environment-climate-change/services/national-wildlife-areas/protected-conserved-areas-database.html) and other effective area-based conservation measures [(OECMs)](https://www.iucn.org/commissions/world-commission-protected-areas/our-work/oecms#:~:text=What%20is%20an%20'OECM'%3F,biodiversity%20outside%20of%20protected%20areas). OECMs are areas other than a protected areas that are managed to sustain biodiversity, ecosystem functions, and cultural, socio-economic, spiritual, and other relevant values^3^.
* Different types of OECMs in B.C. include Old Growth Management Areas, Wildlife Habitat Areas, Nature Reserves, and location-specific examples include the Sea to Sky Wildland Zones, Muskwa-Kechika Special Wildland Areas, and the Flathead Watershed Area.
* For terrestrial areas/inland water, the conserved areas are comprised of `r round(land_pa$summary_total,1)`% PAs and `r round(land_oecm$summary_total,1)`% OECMs.
* Marine areas in B.C. are comprised of `r round(water_pa$summary_total, 1)`% PAs and `r round(water_oecm$summary_total,1)`% OECMs.
* The amount of conserved lands and water is not evenly distributed across B.C. The following provides a glance at the distribution of conserved areas across B.C. and the representation of different ecosystems. 

```{r prot-areas-map, results='asis', fig.alt = "Map of protected lands and waters across B.C.", out.width="80%"}
include_graphics(path = here("out", "prov_map.png"))
```

\vspace{20pt}

## Trends in the Conservation of British Columbia's Terrestrial and Marine Ecoregions

* B.C. is divided into [ecoregions](https://www2.gov.bc.ca/assets/gov/environment/plants-animals-and-ecosystems/ecosystems/broad-ecosystem/an_introduction_to_the_ecoregions_of_british_columbia.pdf). Ecoregions are considered 'big picture' ecosystems and group nearby areas with similar climate and geologic features together. 
* There are `r n_ecoregions[n_ecoregions$type == "land","n"]` terrestrial and `r n_ecoregions[n_ecoregions$type == "water","n"]` marine ecoregions across B.C. 
* The most conserved terrestrial ecoregions are located in the northwest corner of B.C. - `r as.character(land_highest_percent[1,"ecoregion_name"])` and `r as.character(land_highest_percent[2,"ecoregion_name"])` are both over 99% protected as PAs. 
* The least conserved terrestrial ecoregions are the `r as.character(land_lowest_percent[1,"ecoregion_name"])` (`r round(land_lowest_percent[1,"p_region"], 1)`%) and the `r as.character(land_lowest_percent[2,"ecoregion_name"])` (`r round(land_lowest_percent[2,"p_region"], 1)`%).
* The most conserved marine ecoregion is the `r as.character(water_highest_percent[1,"ecoregion_name"])` (`r round(water_highest_percent[1,"p_region"], 1)`%), which consists of `r round(water_highest_percent[water_highest_percent$park_type == "OECM","p_type"], 1)`% OECM. The least conserved is the marine component of the `r as.character(water_lowest_percent[1,"ecoregion_name"])` (`r round(water_lowest_percent[1,"p_region"], 1)`%).

## Terrestrial Ecosystem Representation within Conserved Lands in B.C.

* The distribution of conserved areas is also shown by [biogeoclimatic zones (BEC)](https://www.for.gov.bc.ca/hre/becweb/). 
* BEC zones are defined by the terrestrial ecosystems that develop in an area due to the climate and geography. They provide 
insight into the soils and plant communities you would expect to see in an area. 
* Conserved lands are not evenly distributed among British Columbia's ecosystems. High elevation and mountainous areas such as 
the Boreal Altai Fescue Alpine and the Interior Mountain-heather Alpine zones are over 30% conserved as PA's (`r round(zone_high_elevation_percent[zone_high_elevation_percent$zone_name == "Boreal Altai Fescue Alpine" & zone_high_elevation_percent$park_type == "OECM", "perc_type_zone"], 1)`% and `r round(zone_high_elevation_percent[zone_high_elevation_percent$zone_name == "Interior Mountain-heather Alpine" & zone_high_elevation_percent$park_type == "OECM", "perc_type_zone"], 1)`% OECM respectively) while representing `r ifelse(zone_high_elevation_percent[zone_high_elevation_percent$zone_name == "Boreal Altai Fescue Alpine" & zone_high_elevation_percent$park_type == "OECM", "bec_rep"] > 7, "more", "less")` than 7% of the province's ecosystems. 
* By contrast, low elevation, warm zones such as `r as.character(zone_highest_percent[1, "zone_name"])` are more common across B.C. and tend to be less conserved (< 15% of BEC zone). `r as.character(zone_lowest_percent[1, "zone_name"])` is the least conserved at `r round(zone_lowest_percent[zone_lowest_percent$park_type == "PA", "perc_type_zone"], 1)`% PA.

```{r bec-zone-html, include=is_html, eval=is_html, fig.alt = "Map of the biogeoclimatic zones across B.C.", out.width="100%"}

include_graphics(path = here("out", "bec_map.png"))

pa_bec_sum <- read_rds(paste0(here::here(), "/out/bec_area.rds"))

bec_totals <- pa_bec_sum %>%
    group_by(zone_name) %>% 
    mutate(tooltip = glue(
    "<strong>PA:</strong> ",
    "{format(round(perc_type_zone[park_type == 'PA'], 2), big.mark = ',')} %<br>",
    "<strong>OECM:</strong> ",
    "{format(round(perc_type_zone[park_type == 'OECM'], 2), big.mark = ',')} %")) %>%
    ungroup() %>% 
    dplyr::filter(park_type == "PA") %>%
    mutate(total_bc = bcmaps::bc_area()) %>%
    mutate(bec_rep = total/total_bc) %>%
    select(zone, zone_name, perc_zone, total, total_bc, bec_rep, tooltip) %>%
    arrange(desc(perc_zone))

scatterplot <- ggplot(bec_totals, aes(x=bec_rep, y= perc_zone, label= zone_name))+
    theme_minimal(base_size = 14) +
    #theme(panel.grid.major.y = element_blank()) +
    #geom_point(size=2)+
    geom_point_interactive(aes(color= zone, tooltip=tooltip))+
    ggrepel::geom_text_repel()+
    theme(legend.position = "none", axis.title=element_text(size=12)) +
    scale_color_manual(values = bec_colours(), guide = FALSE) +
    labs(x = "BEC Zone Composition Across B.C. (%)", y = "Percentage of BEC Zone Protected (%)")

girafe(ggobj=scatterplot)
```

```{r}
ld = read_rds(paste0(here::here(), "/out/land_designations.rds"))

prov_terr = ld %>%
  dplyr::filter(type == "land" & designation == "Provincial") %>%
  pull(perc_total)

prov_mar = ld %>%
  dplyr::filter(type == "water" & designation == "Provincial") %>%
  pull(perc_total)

fed_terr = ld %>%
  dplyr::filter(type == "land" & designation == "Federal") %>%
  pull(perc_total) %>%
  .[2]

fed_mar = ld %>%
  dplyr::filter(type == "water" & designation == "Federal") %>%
  pull(perc_total) %>%
  .[2]

pacl_terr = ld %>%
  dplyr::filter(type == "land" & designation == "PACL") %>%
  pull(perc_total) 

pacl_terr_total = sum(pacl_terr)

pacl_mar = ld %>%
  dplyr::filter(type == "water" & designation == "PACL") %>%
  pull(perc_total)

pacl_mar_total = sum(pacl_mar)

ngo_terr = ld %>%
  dplyr::filter(type == "land" & designation == "NGO") %>%
  pull(perc_total)

ngo_mar = ld %>%
  dplyr::filter(type == "water" & designation == "NGO") %>%
  pull(perc_total) 
  
```


## Details of Conserved Land & Water Designations in B.C.

-   **BC Parks (`r round(prov_terr, 1)`% terrestrial; `r round(prov_mar, 1)`% marine)**

    -   Most of the protected land and a third of the protected waters
        in B.C. are managed by [BC
        Parks](http://www.env.gov.bc.ca/bcparks/)^4^.
    -   Protected areas managed by BC Parks are governed by several
        pieces of [legislation](https://bcparks.ca/about/our-mission-responsibilities/legislation/)
        and fall into one of the following designations: [Ecological
        Reserve](https://bcparks.ca/about/our-mission-responsibilities/types-parks-protected-areas/#ec
        logical-reserves), [Provincial 
        Park](https://bcparks.ca/about/our-mission-responsibilities/types-parks-protected-areas/#provin
        cial-parks), [Protected 
        Area](https://bcparks.ca/about/our-mission-responsibilities/types-parks-protected-areas/#protec
        ted-areas), [Conservancy](https://bcparks.ca/about/our-mission-responsibilities/types-parks-pro
        tected-areas/#conservancies), and [Recreation 
        Area](https://bcparks.ca/about/our-mission-responsibilities/types-parks-protected-areas/#recrea
        tion-areas).

-   **National Protected Areas (`r round(fed_terr, 1)`% terrestrial; `r round(fed_mar, 1)`% marine)**

    -   The Government of Canada has established protected land and
        marine areas in British Columbia, for example National Parks,
        National Wildlife Areas, Marine Protected Areas and Migratory
        Bird Sanctuaries.
    -   These designations are governed by several pieces of federal
        legislation including: [*Canada National Parks
        Act*](https://laws-lois.justice.gc.ca/eng/acts/N-14.01/), [*Canada
        National Marine Conservation Areas
        Act*](https://laws-lois.justice.gc.ca/eng/acts/C-7.3/index.html),
        [*Canada Wildlife Act*](https://laws-lois.justice.gc.ca/eng/acts/W-9/), 
        [*Migratory Birds Convention Act*](https://laws-lois.justice.gc.ca/eng/acts/m-7.01/), 
        and the [*Oceans Act (1996)*](http://laws-lois.justice.gc.ca/eng/acts/O-2.4/).

-   **B.C. Provincial Administered Conservation Lands (`r round(pacl_terr_total, 1)`%
    terrestrial; `r round(pacl_mar_total, 1)`% marine)**

    -   [Administered Conservation
        Lands](https://www2.gov.bc.ca/gov/content/environment/plants-animals-ecosystems/wildlife/wildli
        fe-habitats/conservation-lands)
        are lands over which the Government of British Columbia has
        legal administrative and management authority.
    -   Wildlife Management Areas are Administered Conservation Lands
        that are designated under the provincial [*Wildlife
        Act*](https://www.bclaws.gov.bc.ca/civix/document/id/complete/statreg/96488_01) to protect 
        habitat for regionally, nationally or internationally significant species.
    -   Other types of Administered Conservation Lands are aquired by
        way of: [*Land Act*](https://www.bclaws.gov.bc.ca/civix/document/id/complete/statreg/96245_01)
        section 106 Transfers of Administration, Fee Simple Acquisitions
        (through direct purchase, donation, or land exchange), and Lease
        Sites.

-   **B.C. Non-Government Organization Conservation Areas (`r round(ngo_terr, 2)`%
    terrestrial)**

    -   [B.C. Non-Government Organization Conservation
        Areas](https://ltabc.ca/publications-a-research/bc-ngo-conservation-areas-database/), 
        also known as private conservation lands, include (1) Fee Simple areas,
        which refer to ownership of the title to a legal parcel, and (2) Registerable Interests --- other conservation securements registered on title, such as conservation covenants and leases.


## Methods

* This indicator uses data from the [Canadian Protected and Conserved Areas Database](https://www.canada.ca/en/environment-climate-change/services/national-wildlife-areas/protected-conserved-areas-database.html). The [Old Growth Management Areas - Legal - Current](https://catalogue.data.gov.bc.ca/dataset/old-growth-management-areas-legal-current) and the [Wildlife Habitat Areas](https://catalogue.data.gov.bc.ca/dataset/wildlife-habitat-areas-approved) datasets from BC Data Catalogue were also used to fill in missing dates. 
* Municipal and regional parks are not included in the analyses. Overlaps between protected areas have been accounted for in the analyses^5^. 
* The [**R**](http://www.r-project.org) code for repeating the analyses presented on this page is [available on GitHub](https://github.com/bcgov/protected_areas_analysis).
